subject: Capacity & surge guarantees for SparkCloud private pool
messages:
From: Alex Byrne <alex.b@sparkcloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@infra-consult.com>
Date: 2025-05-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity & surge guarantees for SparkCloud private pool

Hi Marissa / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're preparing a procurement request and need to lock a set of throughput guarantees and surge behavior for the private GPU pool we'll host in our AWS VPC. High level asks:

- Sustained throughput target: 2.5M tokens/day (mixed short/long) with 99th pct latency <= 300ms for 1-token streaming responses.
- Burst capacity: ability to absorb 4x baseline for short windows (3–10 min) without errors.
- Warm-pool behavior and warmup time for cold starts (we need guidance on cache warmups).
- Networking: egress caps, per-tenant bandwidth shaping, and expected cross-AZ requirements.

Can you send a short outline of the commitment you can provide (throughput anchors, expected headroom, and what triggers a scale event) plus any timing constraints for procurement/lead times? Also copying Priya from our infra consultancy — she will validate the network topology.

Attachments: none on my side yet — happy to start with a short mutual action plan.

Thanks,
Alex Byrne
Head of Platform — SparkCloud Inc
alex.b@sparkcloud.com
+1 415-555-0198

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Byrne <alex.b@sparkcloud.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity & surge guarantees for SparkCloud private pool

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. I've pulled together an initial sizing workbook and a short commitment outline; see attachment. High-level summary here so your procurement team can review quickly: 

- Baseline commit: we can commit to 2.5M tokens/day sustained across the reserved pool (dedicated partitioning per contract).
- Throughput anchors: sustained (committed) capacity, a "committed headroom" of +40% for predictable bursts, and a separate "surge window" pool that can absorb up to 4x baseline for 5 minutes once per hour without pre-warming. Surge beyond that will be best-effort and subject to additional capacity or failover to hosted models.
- Latency SLO: 99th pct <= 300ms for typical streaming workloads when within committed capacity and with our recommended batching/QoS settings. We include guidance on tokenization mix and batch sizing that materially impacts this.
- Warm-pool behavior: cold-to-warm transition is typically 60–120s depending on model/quantization; we recommend a small always-warm prefix cache for the primary model to meet sub-300ms targets for most requests.
- Network guidance: for your projected throughput pick, reserve at least 20Gbps cross-AZ egress headroom per 250k qps-equivalent lanes, enable VPC ENI scaling per node, and a per-tenant bandwidth bucket to shape noisy tenants.

I've attached: 2025-05-20_Redwood-PrivGPU-sizing.xlsx — it includes run-rate math, burst curves, warm-pool timelines, and a proposed procurement lead-time (4–6 weeks to provision the private pool once contract signed, assuming cloud partner availability). Rafael added commentary below; Jonas will own operational handoffs.

Next steps: if this looks good, we'll create a minimal mutual action plan and a DocuSign for the reserved capacity. Can Priya confirm the VPC limits on your side and any procurement windows?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Byrne <alex.b@sparkcloud.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-05-21T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity & surge guarantees for SparkCloud private pool

Marissa / Alex — quick technical commentary after a first pass on the workbook:

- Sizing anchors: to hit 2.5M tokens/day with 40% headroom our estimate is 6 A100-equivalent GPU slots (depending on model distill/quantization). If SparkCloud will accept a mixed-model variant (smaller quantized for most calls, fall back to FP16 for long-tail), we can reduce slots to 4–5 at the cost of a small hit to tail latency on rare queries.
- Burst model: the 4x burst absorption is doable if you reserve a small warm surge pool (roughly ~20% of baseline) plus short-term admission control. The stateful KV cache is key — recommend a pre-warm window (1–3 min) that we orchestrate from your side during predictable surge events.
- Networking note: cross-AZ egress requirements will scale linearly with qps and model size. For your mix we recommend an initial CIDR mapping and two 10Gbps ENI per GPU node with an autoscale rule to add ENIs at 75% utilization.

Attaching my raw notes: rafael_capacity_notes.txt (small checklist + what to test in soak).

On organization: Jonas — I'll need a contact on your side for testing the warm-pool orchestration and a small spike window to validate warmup times.

Rafael Mendes
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Byrne <alex.b@sparkcloud.com>

Subject: Re: Capacity & surge guarantees for SparkCloud private pool

Thanks Rafael — this is helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from procurement/security: 

- Can you quantify the warm-pool pre-warm bandwidth and explain how we avoid noisy neighbour effects during the warm window?
- For the 4x burst: if we hit sustained 2x for longer than 10 minutes, what is the fallback? (Will traffic be queued, rejected, or will we fail-over to hosted models?)
- Procurement needs a clear lead-time and a cancellation clause if we miss provisioning windows. You mentioned 4–6 weeks; is that guaranteed?

Priya — can you confirm if our VPC has any existing ENI limits that would block the recommended carpet of ENIs per node? Also looping our security reviewer — we will need the network diagrams and egress accounting for the contract.

Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Byrne <alex.b@sparkcloud.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@infra-consult.com>
Date: 2025-05-22T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity & surge guarantees for SparkCloud private pool

Alex — answers inline and next steps below.

> Can you quantify the warm-pool pre-warm bandwidth and explain how we avoid noisy neighbour effects during the warm window?
- Pre-warm traffic: typical pre-warm for a 1–2 minute prefix priming is ~50–150MB per GPU (model dependent). We'll schedule warm-ups as short, targeted prefix calls (not a full dataset pass) to minimize egress. To avoid noisy neighbours we recommend: 1) per-tenant token buckets at the VPC edge, 2) admission control with per-tenant queue lengths, and 3) soft priority for pre-warm orchestration requests.

> For the 4x burst: if we hit sustained 2x for longer than 10 minutes, what is the fallback?
- Fallback behavior: for sustained load beyond the 5–10 minute surge window we'll implement a graded policy: 1) start shedding non-critical traffic (background batch requests), 2) queue low-priority requests up to a configurable latency cap, 3) failover to Redwood hosted models for defined traffic classes if agreed in the contract (we'll include hosted-fallback pricing). We will not silently drop production-critical traffic; shedding and graceful degradation are the plan.

> Procurement lead time and cancellation clause
- Lead-time: 4–6 weeks is our operational target given typical cloud partner availability; we will include a provisioning SLA in the contract with remedies (credits) if we miss agreed windows, subject to cloud partner constraints. Procurement and legal usually accept a clause that ties provisioning SLAs to force-major events and partner capacity.

Next steps:
- I'll circulate a 1-page mutual action plan with the anchors above and the DocuSign link for the reserved capacity term sheet (see HubSpot ticket).
- Rafael / Jonas: coordinate a short soak (2 hours) with SparkCloud next Tuesday to validate warmup times; Rafael's notes have the test checklist.
- Priya: please confirm ENI limits and share the current network diagram with required CIDR ranges.

Thanks — I'll send the MAP and the DocuSign this afternoon.

--
